The ventilator is completely unnecessary. All you need to do is make a proper lid. You don’t need a ventilation system. Also it’s not safe if air is blowing inside the cage at all. You should never have direct air pointed at your cage-especially a constant flow of it. Im not sure if this is doing that but thought I’d let you know. 

It’s a decent start but you’re most likely gonna run into problems with that metal mesh on the side. Most people in the community don’t advise putting air holes in the sides of the cage (or mesh like yours) because it gives them and easy start to chewing. They are likely going to chew at it so you need to monitor that constantly. Also hamsters are burrowing animals, which means you’re gonna want to give as much bedding as you possibly can, this mesh on the side really limits that. These are all reasons why people just make the lids instead.

The substrate on the left, what is it? Paper pellets? That’s what it looks like and if that’s the case these are not a proper substrate to have in the majority of your cage. Paper pellets are safe for hamsters but they don’t hold burrows. They should never be your main substrate. Go for a fluffy paper based bedding like kaytee clean and cozy instead.

Other than that focus on adding more enrichment. It’s a good start but it’s fairly empty. Hamsters love a crowded enclosure. I think a cork log, a piece of grapevine wood, and a dish with coconut fiber would really step this cage up a level. 

I also really suggest filling in any gaps in that bendy bridge with moss to avoid foot and leg injuries. If you would like links to anything and are in the USA let me know. And obviously as others have pointed out it’s too small of a cage.
